newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel plays down Syrian troop movements.
newsitem.headline: Israel plays down Syrian troop movements.

text.p: Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai, trying to calm war jitters in Israel, said on Monday recent Syrian troop movements in Lebanon were no cause for concern.

"We have been following in recent days movements of the Syrian army that took place on the Syrian-Lebanese border," Mordechai told Israeli military correspondents called to the Defence Ministry in Tel Aviv for a special briefing.
"We are weighing the signficance of these movements but in my best judgment, there is no reason for concern," he said in remarks broadcast on Israel and Army radios.

Some 10,000 to 12,000 of Syria's estimated 35,000 troops in Lebanon have redeployed defensively near the Syrian border in recent weeks due to a perceived threat of Israeli attack, Lebanese security sources said on Saturday.

But Israeli media reports have highlighted the troop movements as possible signs that Syria, frustrated over stalled peace talks with Israel over the future of the Golan Heights, might be preparing an attack against the Jewish state.

The redeployment has been the top news in Israel as Yom Kippur, the Jewish Day of Atonement when Syria and Egypt launched surprise attacks 23 years ago, approaches. The fast day is observed, according to the Hebrew calendar, on September 23.

"Of course we will not be surprised (again). We are following events and taking all the necessary measures," Mordechai said, without elaborating. "But if you ask me if the recent verbal escalation has been justified, I would say no."
Syria has repeatedly rejected Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's proposal to resume peace talks, saying it did not contain a commitment to trading land for peace.
Israel's previous Labour-led government broke off negotiations with Syria after Moslem suicide bombers killed 59 people in the Jewish state last February and March.
The United States has been trying to find a formula to resume the talks, deadlocked over the future of the Golan Heights.
Netanyahu has said Israel must maintain sovereignty over the northern plateau it captured from Syria in the 1967 Middle East war. Syria wants Israel to return all of the Golan.

In Lebanon, most of the re-deployed troops had taken up positions in the mountain range on the Syrian border where the Syrian army has SAM-7 anti-aircraft missiles and anti-aircraft gun batteries installed, the Lebanese security sources said.
The re-deployment has become more visible in the past week with the Syrians pulling out of several landmark positions they maintained for years in and around Beirut.

Despite the pullouts, armed Syrian troops are still stationed in the Lebanese capital and are highly visible in some areas, including Shi'ite Moslem suburbs that are a stronghold of the pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God).
